extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors preparing papers with AMS-LATEX (users with some TEX/LaTeX experience)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, example-driven instructions for preparing mathematical documents using the amsart AMS‑LaTeX documentstyle, including preamble setup, theorem/proof environments, equations, cross-references, bibliographies, diagrams, macros, and a template file.

rubrics_metrics.name: The \documentstyle command and its options
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any visible content, include a \documentstyle command (e.g. \documentstyle{amsart}). Optional arguments control default font size and included packages, e.g. [12pt], [amscd] (commutative diagram macros), and [amssymb] (AMSFonts special symbols). Optional args are separated by commas, with no spaces inside square brackets; order doesn’t matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \documentstyle[12pt]{amsart}, \documentstyle[amscd]{amsart}, \documentstyle[12pt,amscd,amssymb]{amsart}. Note that the amscd macros aren't included by default because of memory; include amscd only when using CD diagrams. The documentstyle choice determines whether you are using AMS‑LATEX (amsart/amsbook) or standard LaTeX (article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble vs document body: \begin{document} and \end{document}
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything to appear in the document must be between \begin{document} and \end{document}. Macro definitions are allowed before \begin{document} (in the preamble). Anything after \end{document} is ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put \newcommand definitions and other setup in the preamble. There are no optional arguments for \begin{document}/\end{document}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectioning commands and labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \section{...}, \subsection{...}, \subsubsection{...} to create sections; starred forms like \section*{...} produce unnumbered sections. To reference a section you must label it with \label{key}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \section{Basic \LaTeX\ stuff}\label{sec:basicstuff} so you can write Section~\ref{sec:basicstuff}. Subsubsections exist; there is a \subsubsection* for unnumbered ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels take the number of the smallest enclosing structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The \label{key} command assigns the key the value of the smallest enclosing numbered structure (section, subsection, theorem, equation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus a \label inside Section 5 but outside any subsection yields '5', while a \label inside Section 5.1 yields '5.1'. For theorems and equations, labels pick up those numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: use \em, not explicit font switches
rubrics_metrics.description: To emphasize text (italics), use the \em command rather than switching to italics explicitly; \em toggles based on current font.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The whole is {\em more\/} than the sum of its parts. In theorem bodies (slanted font) \em will switch you back to upright as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references require multiple LaTeX runs (.aux and .toc behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX writes an .aux file each run with keys used for cross-references; you usually must run LaTeX twice (or three times if using a table of contents) to resolve all references. LaTeX prints a warning at the end of a run if labels have changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First run creates .aux/.toc files; second run fills refs; a large table of contents that changes page breaks may require a third run. Ignore 'undefined label' warnings on the first run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title, running title, author, address, email, and \maketitle
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \title[Optional running title]{Actual title} for title and running head, \author{...} for each author, \address{...} for addresses, \email{...} (use @@ in source to get @), and \thanks{...} for acknowledgements. After these give \maketitle to typeset the title block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line breaks in title/address use \\; use optional short title for running heads. In amsart the author address is printed at the end of the paper. For multiple authors, give separate \author and \address commands; use initials in running head for multi-author conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date command
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \date{...} to set the date; \date{\today} inserts the processing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the \date command before \maketitle if you want a date printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem-like environments (thm, prop, lem, cor, defn, rem, ex, notation, terminology, bigthm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and use theorem environments with \begin{thm} ... \end{thm} (or \begin{prop}, \begin{lem}, etc.). bigthm is numbered separately as Theorem A, B, ... Notation and Terminology are unnumbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can give an optional argument to name a theorem: \begin{thm}[Pythagorus] ... For labeling, place \label inside the theorem environment. The template demonstrates these environment definitions and their typical printed forms and font shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof environments (pf and pf*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \begin{pf} ... \end{pf} to typeset a proof, which prints 'Proof.'; use \begin{pf*}{Proof (sufficiency)} ... \end{pf*} to replace the default 'Proof' heading with custom text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \begin{pf*}{Proof of Theorem~\ref{pythagthm}} ... yields 'Proof of Theorem 4.1.' The pf* environment requires a second argument to \begin{pf*}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing theorem body fonts and theoremstyles
rubrics_metrics.description: The amsart style provides theoremstyles: plain, definition, and remark. The font used in theorem bodies is set by \theorembodyfont when the \newtheorem command is given. Grouping (\begingroup ... \endgroup) confines changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template uses \theoremstyle{plain} then \begingroup \theorembodyfont{\sl} ... \endgroup to make theorem bodies slanted. To use italics, remove the \theorembodyfont command. Use \renewcommand{\thebigthm}{\Alph{bigthm}} for alphabetical numbering of bigthm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing equations: \label, \eqref, and equation vs equation*
rubrics_metrics.description: To number an equation use the equation environment; to leave it unnumbered use equation*. Label equations with \label{key} and refer with \eqref{key} (prints number with parentheses and upright font).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed math can also be made with $$...$$, \[...\], or \begin{displaymath}...\end{displaymath}. Use \eqref instead of \ref for equation numbers to ensure parentheses and upright font are correct regardless of surrounding font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline mathematics: $...$ or \(...\)
rubrics_metrics.description: Put inline math between $...$ or use \(...\) as an alternative which provides slightly more error checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: This is true for $i+j\le n$ is equivalent to This is true for \(i+j\le n\). Either is acceptable; \( \) can help catch errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed mathematics: various environments and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Several alternatives for displayed math: $$...$$, \[...\], \begin{displaymath}...\end{displaymath}, \begin{equation*}...\end{equation*} (unnumbered), and \begin{equation}...\end{equation} (numbered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose equation vs equation* depending on whether you want a number. Use \label inside a numbered environment to reference the equation later with \eqref.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS-LATEX multiline display environments (reference to User's Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS-LATEX supplies environments to typeset complicated multiline displays (e.g., align-like structures); see the AMS-LATEX User's Guide for full details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document references the User's Guide and sample files (testart.tex) for examples and detailed usage (pp.26–30 and pp.30–42 in sample).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutative diagrams (CD environment) and amscd option
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the CD environment inside displayed math to draw rectangular commutative diagrams. To use CD, include the amscd option in \documentstyle (e.g. \documentstyle[...,amscd]{amsart}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrows: @>>> right, @<<< left, @AAA up, @VVV down, @= horizontal equals, @| vertical equals. End lines with \\ except the last. Diagrams must be inside a displayed math environment; using equation will number the whole display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling and placing labels on CD arrows; invisible arrows and partial rows
rubrics_metrics.description: In CD, for horizontal arrows anything between the first and second > is above the arrow, and between second and third > is below it. For vertical arrows use multiple V's similarly. Use @. (at + period) for an invisible arrow (to omit a column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: @>f_*> places f_* above a right arrow. To omit the beginning of a line use @.; to leave off the right end of a line end the line early with \\.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro definitions: prefer \newcommand/\renewcommand over \def
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \newcommand{\tensor}{\otimes}; \newcommand{\pushout}[3]{#1\cup_{#2}#3}. If overriding a preexisting command, use \renewcommand. Avoid plain TeX \def as it lacks checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: List environments: itemize, enumerate, description
rubrics_metrics.description: Use itemize for bulleted lists, enumerate for numbered lists, and description for labeled items (\item[term]...). Environments may be nested and enumerate will track nesting level and number style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show wrapping items and nested enumerate producing (a),(b),(c) at the second level. Description prints the argument followed by a colon-style layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: The bibliography environment and \bibitem entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the bibliography with \begin{thebibliography}{number} where number is a sample widest printed number; each item is \bibitem{key}Item entry. Use \cite{key} to reference items in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'number' argument helps LaTeX compute width of the item labels; e.g. use {10} if you have 10–19 items. \cite optionally takes a second argument for annotation: \cite[Chapter I]{HA} prints as [6, Chapter I].

rubrics_metrics.name: Template file and recommended preamble setup
rubrics_metrics.description: The template.tex provides a ready preamble: documentstyle options, macro definitions, theorem environment declarations, and commands like \numberwithin{equation}{section}. Put macros in the preamble and follow template conventions for theorem styles and numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template demonstrates grouping to confine \theorembodyfont, \newtheorem definitions, \renewcommand{\thebigthm}{\Alph{bigthm}}, and where to place \maketitle, \tableofcontents, and sectioning commands. Use the template as a mostly ready-to-use starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering equations within sections: \numberwithin{equation}{section}
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \numberwithin{equation}{section} to make equation numbers include the section number (e.g., (6.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place this in the preamble; it affects how equations are numbered across the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of starred environments for unnumbered forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Many environments have starred variants that omit numbering, e.g. \section*{...}, \subsubsection*{...}, \begin{equation*}...\end{equation*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the starred forms when you do not want numbers (e.g., for unnumbered sections or displays).
